reader.requirement: At --std 85 the compiler must not judge library text on its own: COPY (and REPLACE) are fully processed first, and syntax is checked only on the resultant program, so library text that is a fragment, or not COBOL until REPLACING/REPLACE rewrites it, is accepted when the result is valid and diagnosed when it is not.

reader.notes: The frontend expands every COPY and REPLACE before lexing and parsing, so library text is only ever judged inside the resultant program. Probes with fragments, replaced-away non-COBOL text and an invalid result all behave as GR8 requires.

refuter.evidence: Code: src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Frontend/Preprocessor/CopyProcessor.cs#ResolveOneCopy computes `libraryHoldsCopy = FindStatementKeyword(normalized, 0, "COPY")` on the library text BEFORE ApplyReplacements, and at !edition.Has(2002) raises Constructs.CopyNestedLibraryText2002 (COBOL0900) citing §1985:XII.2.4 GR12, whose text judges 'The text produced as a result of the complete processing of a COPY statement', i.e. AFTER REPLACING. So at --std 85 the library text's correctness IS determined independently, which GR8 says cannot be done. Probe refute-1985-04/c4/r4a.cob at --std 85: library NESTZ.cpy = 'COPY ZZZ.'; source 'COPY NESTZ REPLACING ==COPY ZZZ== BY ==MOVE 3 TO X==.' The produced text is 'MOVE 3 TO X.' (no COPY), valid; the compiler prints COBOL0900 'library text that contains a COPY statement requires COBOL-2002 ... COPY NESTZ' (plus COBOL2451, below). Probes that UPHOLD the rest: r4b (COPY inside a literal and a comment line in library text) runs and prints 'COPY ZZZ.'; r4e (COPY in an AUTHOR comment-entry inside library text, §1985:XII.2.3 SR10) runs; r4c (a REPLACE statement in library text, then applied to later source) prints AFTER-REPLACE; r4d (REPLACING ==XX== BY ==COPY== producing a COPY statement) is refused, as GR12 requires. THE READING this rests on: pseudo-text ==COPY ZZZ== carrying no separator period is not 'a COPY statement' (§1985:XII.2.3 SR2 makes the period part of one), so SR7 does not bar it, and SR6 excludes COPY only as word-1/word-2. The compiler also refuses that pseudo-text on its own (r4g: a REPLACING ==COPY ZZZ== that matches nothing gives COBOL2451 citing §2023:7.2.3.3 SR1); if SR7 is read to bar it, no legal 1985 program reaches the pre-replacement check and the verdict would stand. cite.py: OK §1985:XII.2.4 GR8 ('The syntactic correctness of the library text cannot be independently determined'); OK §1985:XII.2.4 GR12 ('The text produced as a result of the complete processing of a COPY statement must not contain a COPY statement'); OK §1985:XII.2.3 SR2 ('terminated by the separator period'); OK §1985:XII.2.3 SR6 ('any single COBOL word except'); OK §1985:XII.2.3 SR7 ('a COPY statement must not occur within a COPY statement'). Known note: kb/Work/PB5126 (landed) introduced this 85 gate for library text that holds a COPY; it does not treat a COPY that REPLACING removes.
edition-sites-missed: src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Frontend/Preprocessor/CopyProcessor.cs#ResolveOneCopy: the reader listed it for the GR12 gate but not that the gate's 85 arm tests the pre-REPLACING library text (`normalized`), not the produced text; at 2002+ the same test feeds the REPLACING+nested-COPY refusal (COBOL1640), which 2023's GR10 states on the library text
refuter.corrected: PARTIAL (rejects-legal-source, cause a): at --std 85 the GR12 nested-COPY gate must examine the text produced after REPLACING, not the library text alone; a COPY in library text that REPLACING replaces away is refused (COBOL0900), so the library text is judged independently, contrary to GR8. At --std 2023 the same program is refused by COBOL1640/COBOL2451, which the 2023 text (7.2.3.4 GR10) does state on the library text. Companion item (separate rule §1985:XII.2.3 SR7): COBOL2451 refuses the word COPY inside pseudo-text.
